name: Mathematics for AI and LLMs
audience: Engineers, architects and technical leaders who want to really understand how models learn and how LLMs compute, and explain it with confidence. High-school algebra assumed; everything else is built up.
format: This site's course with a 40-question practice test mixing concept, calculation and judgment questions.
scenarios: Explaining embeddings and similarity search to a team
Debugging a training run that diverges
Sizing GPU memory for an LLM
Designing an eval and judging if a difference is real
verifyNotes: This is the site's own deep-foundations course, not a vendor certification: there are no exam facts to confirm, so spend Research on finding the best official/primary sources per topic (URLs that will be cited as sources) and on current library APIs. Goal: the learner should be able to explain and derive these ideas confidently in an interview or design review. Lessons go deep: intuition first, then the formal definition, then a fully worked numeric example, then exactly where it shows up in modern AI/LLMs, then a common misconception. Write math in LaTeX between double dollars only: $$...$$ (inline or on its own line for display); NEVER single-dollar math (single $ renders literally). In JSON strings escape backslashes (\\frac). Code in fenced ```python blocks that run as-is. Every lesson has a hands-on lab: a small Python exercise with the expected output. Question mix: ~40% concept/judgment, ~35% compute-or-predict (give numbers or code, ask for the result), ~25% debug-or-choose-the-right-approach. Verifiers MUST run every compute and code-output question with {{root}}/.pipeline/py/bin/python (Python 3.9 with NumPy 2.0, pandas 2.3, scikit-learn 1.6, PyTorch 2.8). Code that uses Python 3.10+ syntax (match, X | Y unions, 3.12 type-parameter syntax) cannot run there: label such items "(Python 3.10+)" in the stem and verify them by careful reasoning against docs.python.org and fix keys that disagree; state any randomness seed in the stem. Sources: official library docs and primary/canonical teaching material only (see src/content/official-domains.json, track "foundations"); no blogs or Medium. Check every formula and worked example numerically in Python. Use canonical notation (e.g. attention = softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k)) V, cross-entropy, KL). For memory/FLOP estimates state the assumptions (bytes per parameter, 2N FLOPs per token for a forward pass, ~6N per token for training).

domains.name: Linear algebra for embeddings and models
skills: Vectors, norms, dot product, cosine similarity and why embeddings are compared with them
Matrices as linear maps; matrix multiplication and shape reasoning (batch x seq x dim)
Transpose, inverse, rank, linear independence, projections
Eigenvalues/eigenvectors, SVD and PCA; low-rank approximation and why LoRA works
Tensors and broadcasting as the language of deep learning

domains.name: Calculus and optimisation
skills: Derivatives, partial derivatives, gradients and directional derivatives
Chain rule, computational graphs and backpropagation by hand
Jacobians, Hessians and curvature intuition
Gradient descent, learning rate, SGD and mini-batches, momentum, Adam/AdamW, weight decay, schedules and warmup
Convexity, local minima, saddle points, vanishing/exploding gradients, gradient clipping

domains.name: Probability and statistics
skills: Random variables, distributions (Bernoulli, categorical, Gaussian), expectation and variance
Conditional probability, independence and Bayes’ theorem with base rates
Maximum likelihood and MAP; why training minimises negative log-likelihood
Sampling, law of large numbers, central limit theorem, standard error
Confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, p-values, multiple comparisons and A/B tests for model evals

domains.name: Information theory, losses and decoding
skills: Logits, softmax, sigmoid and log-sum-exp stability
Entropy, cross-entropy, KL divergence and their relationship
Perplexity and bits per token
Temperature, top-k, top-p and greedy decoding as operations on a distribution
Common losses and metrics: MSE, cross-entropy, precision/recall/F1, calibration

domains.name: The mathematics of transformers and LLMs
skills: Tokens, embedding matrices and positional information (sinusoidal, RoPE)
Scaled dot-product attention step by step, causal masking, multi-head attention
Residual connections, layer normalisation, MLP blocks; parameter counting
Compute and memory arithmetic: FLOPs per token, scaling laws (Kaplan, Chinchilla), KV-cache size, context length cost
Numerics: fp32/fp16/bf16, quantisation (int8/int4) and its error
